title: super-roast report body rule and format repair
description:
Split from super-plan-2s3 (spec docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups-design.md §4.1 b, c — super-roast side). owns: super-roast report body rule and format-repair step; owns: repaired-report file naming (…-format-repair.md) and its recording as the round's path in roast-code:/roast-design:, which collection reads. consumes: the spec §4.1 report grammar as super-plan-mlr.1 enforces it; the whole-file rule wording from super-plan-2s3 is restated, not imported (parity checked in the integration sweep). A format repair is format-only: the round's reviewReadiness, inputs and finding content are unchanged.
Files: skills/super-roast/reporter-prompt.md (Step 6 template ~L221-285), skills/super-roast/SKILL.md (template mirror ~L195-216 and the step that writes reportMarkdown ~L218-220), skills/super-auto/SKILL.md phase-4 row only if it restates the write step, tests (prompt-text assertion + report-verdict fixtures).
Investigation: docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/investigation/inv-2s3.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every section of the reporter template (Confirmed findings, Not verified sections, Beyond remainder cap, Rejected, Unverified nits, Escalations) states: only "- " items with indented continuations, or "- none"; no prose preamble, sub-headings or bold labels inside; any explanatory sentence goes outside recognized sections. SKILL.md mirror matches.
- [ ] After writing reportMarkdown, the orchestrator runs `report-verdict --complete --source format-check <file>` on it; only on exit 4 (grammar failure; exit 2 usage/I/O errors never trigger a repair) it re-dispatches the reporter once with the parser error and the original path and writes the result to a new sibling …-format-repair.md (never over the original). The repair is accepted only when (i) it passes --complete, (ii) its header block (every line before the first `## ` heading) is byte-identical to the original's, (iii) `report-verdict --keys` output is identical for both files, and (iv) every original line starting a list item (`- ` or `* `) appears unchanged in the repair. An accepted repair is recorded as the round's report and "report format repair: <original> → <repair> — <error>" is appended to the friction log; if any check fails, the original is recorded and the friction line names the failed check. The orchestrator never edits finding content.
- [ ] Tests: the retained pr1/roast-pr-1 Unverified-nits shape fails --complete today (exit 4 once super-plan-mlr.1 lands) and a template-shaped fixture exits 0 with all items; prompt-text assertions cover the body rule and the repair step.
- [ ] skills/super-roast/super-roast-workflow.md is not changed; if a change proves necessary, its documented dryRun scenarios are re-run and the agent counts match the doc.
- [ ] Prompt-text or fixture tests cover repair rejection: a repair that drops a list item, changes a header line or changes --keys output is not recorded.

title: Report extractor: reject sub-headings inside recognized sections
description:
Split from super-plan-2s3 (spec docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups-design.md §4.1 d): a sub-heading or bold-label line inside a recognized report section that already has items currently ends the section and silently drops the items after it with exit 0 (repro: printf '## Must fix
- a
### detail
- b
' | report-verdict --complete returns only a). Make it an error in both grammar copies.
owns: report-verdict --complete section grammar in both copies (skills/super-code/scripts/report-verdict and assembly-archive.cjs strictDraft), incl. the no-sub-heading rule decided in spec §4.1; consumes: nothing from siblings. super-plan-2s3 and super-plan-mlr.2 write producer text against the same spec-decided rule.
Files: skills/super-code/scripts/report-verdict (--complete section boundary ~L86-131), skills/super-code/scripts/assembly-archive.cjs (strictDraft ~L13-36), tests/super-code/test-report-verdict.sh, plus any existing assembly-archive test.
Investigation: docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/investigation/inv-2s3.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] report-verdict --complete exits 4 (the new distinct grammar-failure exit, spec §4.1(c)) with a message naming the section when a sub-heading or bold label follows items inside a recognized section; no items are dropped silently.
- [ ] Discriminator (spec §4.1(d)), for a heading()-matched line inside a recognized section with items: a recognized section label (that copy's word list, any level, ATX or bold) is a sibling; an ATX heading at the same or shallower level than the section's opening heading is a sibling; a deeper ATX heading or an unrecognized bold label is the forbidden sub-heading. A bold-label-opened section ends at any ATX heading or recognized bold label. Fixtures cover back-to-back recognized sections, `## Findings` then `## Analysis`, and `### detail` / `**Note**` after items.
- [ ] Every --complete grammar failure (unrecognized source, missing verdict, missing/empty section, unmarked text, forbidden sub-heading) exits 4; usage errors, invalid source id and unreadable/non-file/invalid-UTF-8 artifacts keep exit 2; stderr prefix `report-verdict: --complete: ` unchanged; the usage comment documents both codes.
- [ ] assembly-archive.cjs strictDraft applies the same rule and discriminator (as a thrown grammar error).
- [ ] The same sub-heading fixtures run against both copies in tests and both reject.
- [ ] Existing conforming fixtures and the footer-only controls still exit 0; existing report-verdict tests pass.

title: Review continuity followups (mosh triage P1/P2)
description:
Root epic for super-auto run docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/ (branch super-auto/review-continuity-followups). Spec: docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups-design.md. Literal human request: "lets $ht handoff to claude-2 all p1 and p2 fixes, at once, using /super-auto in fully autonomous mode, both roasts on". Closable by this run: it holds exactly the seven followups plus run-created leaves.

## Global Constraints
- Smallest change covering each issue, in existing scripts/prompts/contracts/tests; no new workflow abstraction (source: coordinator scope choice relayed with the human request).
- Tests prove behavior (run the real script / rendered prompt against fixtures), not mirror implementation text (source: project instruction, coordinator brief).
- Never overwrite original review reports or archives; never blind-reset, force-delete, stash or WIP-commit task work (source: bead acceptance super-plan-2s3, super-plan-v94).
- Never infer finding resolution from bead closure, equal display key or a later clean review; never auto-approve a human acceptance change (source: bead acceptance super-plan-row).
- No global hardcoded AI-trailer ban, no history rewrite, no metadata-lint framework (source: bead acceptance super-plan-zhk).
- dryRun agent counts recorded in skills/super-code/coordinator-workflow.md must not change (source: project release instruction).
- Commit messages: Conventional-commit style matching repo history (e.g. 'fix(super-code): ...'). This repo's instruction files set no trailer policy.
- Skill-text edits stay minimal and do not rewrite carefully tuned content (Red Flags, rationalization lists, 'human partner' wording) (source: CLAUDE.md Skill Changes Require Evaluation).
<!-- key-abstractions digest: begin -->
- Range relevance rule: decides whether a run.md is in the captured range using paths and mirror-origin status only, evaluated after origin authentication; a new relevance criterion goes in this one predicate; callers never test changed paths or run ids themselves.
- Run-scoped gap sink: routes each run-attributed problem to `gaps` or `outOfRange`, buffering until origins are authenticated; any new per-run validation reports through it; callers never push to `gaps` directly for a run-scoped problem.
- `claude_window`: maps a model id to its window in bash, kept in step with `CLAUDE_WINDOWS` by the parity test; a new model is a row here and in `context-pass.mjs` plus its parity ids; callers never add their own case list of 1M ids.
- Bookkeeping completeness checks: surface missing `finding-route` and `finding-source` records as projection gaps; any new missing-record check is added to this pass; callers never use a key match to link or resolve a finding.
<!-- key-abstractions digest: end -->

title: Revalidate reused stacked task branches against current prerequisites
description:
Source: Herdr mosh Phase2 report mnSGIFED8uqR, alepar/herdr@a900f96707d42ba28fdec87a1fc03afbb12a7b31. Triage source Superpowers 444f86b2 (6.6). Evidence /private/tmp/superpowers-mosh-phase2-triage-9tg. Report records mosh-hex.5 SETUP_FAILED after reuse of stale pre-review parent. Current coordinator workspaceSetup BOTH-exist path explicitly reuses branch/worktree as-is, while stackStep only runs for fresh setup; recut state is invocation-local. Static reuse gap confirmed, incident prior refs/setup output not retained here; requested existing evidence, no rerun.

## Design slice (run super-plan-mlr, spec docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups-design.md §4.5)
owns: workspaceSetup reuse reconciliation text (shared stack-merge helper used by fresh stackStep and drift rebuild). consumes: nothing from siblings. The drift rebuild creates only "stack: p" merge commits with the coordinator's fixed message, like the fresh stack step; they are not implementer commits and are outside super-plan-zhk's scope.
oldBase rule (spec §4.5): the existing both-exist base rule — newest first-parent stack: commit on the task branch, else git merge-base <branch> <integration>.
Files: skills/super-code/coordinator.js (workspaceSetup ~L2624-2645, stackStep ~L2631-2633), skills/super-code/coordinator-workflow.md (~L902-903, ~L1147-1169), skills/super-code/coordinator-subagents.md (~L57), tests/super-code/test-dispatch-text.sh (setup text assertions), a real-git fixture test modelled on tests/super-code/test-setup-cleanup.sh.
Out of scope: seeding discardFailed for a resumed cancelled line (follow-up).
Investigation: docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/investigation/inv-v94.md.
acceptance_criteria:
Original acceptance: exercise retry/resume with changed prerequisite and existing task branch; detect/reconcile drift before implementer dispatch, preserving committed and dirty work; no blind reset/delete; distinguish verified code gap from unproven historical cause.
- [ ] Both-exist ordinary path checks drift (a current parent not an ancestor of the task branch, or a first-parent stack: X commit for X no longer a current parent); no drift → unchanged reuse.
- [ ] Drift + dirty worktree (ignoring .tmp/) → SETUP_FAILED "prerequisite drift; uncommitted work preserved; nothing reset"; files untouched.

description:

## Design slice (run super-plan-mlr, spec docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups-design.md §4.2)
owns: Range relevance rule; owns: Run-scoped gap sink (see epic digest); owns: review-inputs.json outOfRange field (informational list, never counted in status or gaps); owns: review-inputs.json status/gaps semantics after range scoping. consumes: nothing from siblings.
Files: skills/super-code/scripts/dispatch-text.mjs (reviewInputs ~L129-408: snapshot loop, validateCollections, authenticateOrigins, result object), skills/super-auto/SKILL.md (§Review collection, one clause on range scoping), tests/super-code/test-dispatch-text.sh and/or tests/super-auto/test-scripts.sh.
Prototype diff and scenario script (from investigation, verify before reuse): docs/superpowers/runs/2026-10-28-review-continuity-followups/investigation/rsc-proto.diff, rsc-scenarios.sh; findings inv-rsc.md.
acceptance_criteria:
Original acceptance: later unrelated product-only range is not blocked solely by untouched old collections; preserve provenance guards for relevant claimed, changed, deleted or corrupt artifacts and real omissions; do not blanket-filter by current run ID or waive inherited gaps.
- [ ] Relevance is decided by one predicate from the captured changed paths: current run; run.md path, its run.md.collection-origin.json sidecar, or any path at/under dirname(run)/reviews/ changed; or re-read as a mirror origin.
- [ ] Problems from irrelevant runs go to a non-blocking outOfRange list in review-inputs.json and the provenance digest, labelled informational; they never change status or exit code; irrelevant runs are still parsed for the mirror ambiguity check.
- [ ] Evaluation order (spec §4.2): the sink buffers run-attributed problems from snapshot and origin authentication and classifies them once, after authenticateOrigins has run at both endpoints (before validateCollections of the endpoints); later problems are classified immediately. Every run named as origin by a mirror declaration that authenticateOrigins examined counts as re-read (authenticated or not). Test: a mirror-origin run with a snapshot problem outside the changed paths still blocks (exit 3).
- [ ] Tests (real git fixtures): A product-only range with an untouched incomplete prior run exits 0 with outOfRange non-empty; B range edits that run.md → exit 3; C range edits a file under its reviews/ → exit 3; D range corrupts it → exit 3; E range deletes the corrupt run.md → exit 3; F broad range whose base predates the prior run → exit 3; current run with incomplete history stays guarded.
- [ ] Existing review-inputs suites still pass (current-review-selection.mjs, collection-origin-selection.mjs, failed-assembly-archive.mjs, selection-recovery-correction.mjs and the -r1.sh suites listed in inv-rsc.md).
